rule: A chain registered as held out in HELDOUT.json never reaches a fix: its roots are kernel-denied and refused as inputs, its id is refused for tuning, and a fix naming it is refused until the chain is retired by a committed registry edit.
chose: 4.1 is enforced by the evaluator through a committed registry, sofar-evaluator HELDOUT.json, which names held-out chains by IDENTITY only: chain id, root paths, commit shas. Chain L is registered with ~/IO/bench-sealed, ~/IO/tallybox-ledger and ~/IO/tallybox-reference-l, and no shas yet. Enforcement: (1) every root joins the candidate profile's unreadable set and gets a self-test deny probe; (2) a root is refused as an evaluator input (--repo, --brief, --loss-study, a candidate's repo); (3) a held-out chain id is refused where a tuning chain is chosen; (4) a loss row or brief that names a held-out chain ("chain L"/"CHAIN-L"), root or sha is refused; (5) a held-out sha in a fix transcript voids the fix, while names and paths only warn. Retiring a chain is a committed edit that moves it from `heldout` to `retired` with a reason. A retired chain may be used for tuning and is refused as a release proof (releaseChainRefusal, for 4.2). Every run.json records the registry's sha256.
over: (a) Separation by convention, trusting fix-builders not to look: the operator asked for an exclusion the evaluator enforces. (b) Voiding a fix transcript on the chain's name or path: sofar's own record names chain L legitimately (memory-lead 5.2, chain-l-author), so a fix agent reading its record would void every fix. (c) Automatic retirement when a held-out mention is seen: retirement changes what counts as a release proof, so it is a reviewable commit, never a side effect. (d) Reading the chain to derive its shas: the fix-builder stays blind; the author or operator adds them.
because: A held-out chain's value is that no fix saw it. Only the evaluator is present at every point where tuning could touch the release chain: the kernel profile, the inputs, the chain choice and the transcript. So the rule is enforced there, and a malformed registry refuses rather than permits.
